<khat>, one, and <suak>, be born, come out or become, written as one word at the end of a headline: one such person or animal has been born or has come to be
<khat>, one, and <sung>, in, written as one word after a noun: inside one thing, as {mawtaw khatsung ah}, in one car, or within one unit of time, as {Minute khatsung in}, within a minute
<khat>, one, and <sungah>, inside, written as one word after a noun: inside one thing, as {Box khatsungah}, in one box
<khatsung>, in one, and <pan>, from, written as one word after a noun: from within one, as {innkuan khatsungpan}, from one family
<khat>, one, with the distributive ending {-ta}: one for each, one at a time
one person alone, without company; {khattang kisa} is feel lonely
<khat> and <tawh> written as one word, after a noun: with a, with one, by means of one
<khat> with plural {-te}, in {pawl khatte} and {kim khatte}, some people, some of them
<khat> with plural {-te} at the end of a number that counts a group, as {za khatte}, the hundred, and {sawm-le-khatte}, the eleven
<khat>, one, with <teh>, here a spoken form of <ciangin>, written as one word: at or in one, as {nipi khatteh}, in a week, and {hun khatteh}, at one time, after a time
<khat>, one, and <tek>, each, written as one word: one for each person
<khat>, one, with <thu> and the ending <in>: all at one time; {ni khatthu-in} is in one single day
<khat>, one, with <tuak>, each, written as one word after a noun: one for each of them
<khat>, one, with <tung>, on, written as one word and followed by <ah> or <panin>: on one, as {Motorcycle khattung ah}, on one motorcycle; of a person, against one
<khattung>, on one, with the place marker <ah>, written as one word: on one vehicle, or leaning on one person
<khat>, one, and <tungpan>, from, written as one word and placed after a noun: from a person or from on a thing, as {numei khattungpan}, from a woman
<khat> and <val> written as one word: more than one; after a unit, over one of it, as {Million khatval}, over a million
one time, from <khat>, one, and <vei>, time; with <kik> on the verb it means once more, and at the start of a story it means on one occasion

terms: once or twice/a time or two
definition: <khatvei>, once, and <nihvei>, twice, said together without a linking word: once or twice, a few times only; stands before the verb, often followed by <bek>, only
<khatvei>, once, and <bek>, only, written as one word
<khatvei>, once, and the emphatic <mah>, written as one word: one time, with <ngei> once before and with <kik> or <leuleu> once again
<khatvei>, once, with the ending <na>: the first time something is done
<khatvei>, once, with the distributive <ta>, each, written as one word after a period of time: once in every such period, as in {khakhat in khatveita}, once a month
<khatvei> once, with <vei> repeated: now and then
<khatvei> and <zong> written as one word: even once; with a negative verb, never, not a single time
one of two as against the other; mostly {a khatzaw}, the other one, and {khatzaw zaw}, either one of the two

terms: either one/any one/one or the other
definition: <khat>, one, with <zawkzawk>: one of those named, whichever it is; placed after a list or after <lak>, among
<khatzaw> with <pa> for a man, written as one word: the other of two men, mostly as {adang khatzawpa}
<khatzaw>, the other of two, and the topic marker <pen> written as one word: as for the other one
<khat> and <zawzaw> written as one word: whichever one of two
<khat>, one, with <zong>, even; with {om lo} it means there is not even one
in statements that are not negative: one more of the kind as well, as in {Police Officer khatzong liam}, one police officer was also injured; with <ahihi> it is also one of them
a rope, cord, string or thread of any thickness; {khau dum} is a blue cord and {sihna khau} the cords of death
<khau> and <bang> written as one word: like a cord, a simile of songs and poetic speech for what is drawn out, traced or entangled
<khau>, cord, with <dum>, blue: a blue cord or blue thread
<khau>, rope, with <gui>, vine: a climbing or trailing plant with long stems like cords, also used for tying
hard, firm or strong, not giving way; {lung khauh} and {lungsim khauh} mean stubborn or hard-hearted, and {khauh takin} means firmly or severely
<khauh> written with a capital in a heading, {Itna in Sihna Zahin Khauh}, love is as strong as death
<khauh>, hard, with the ending <in>; after <lung> or <lungsim> it means stubbornly, with a hard heart
<khauh>, strong, with <kik>, again: become strong again
<khauh> and <lua> written as one word: very or too strong, said of wind, an earthquake, fire, a smell or speed
<khauh>, strong, and <mahmah>, very, written as one word: very strong, said of wind, a smell, smoke, an illness or a crackdown
<khauh>, hard, with the ending <na>: the quality of being hard or unyielding; {lungsim khauhna} is stubbornness of heart, and in Philippians 3:6 it stands for zeal
<khauh>, hard, with <pa>, the man; {thu khauhpa} is the harsh, fierce man
<khauh> strong, with <pah>, at once
strong and forceful, or growing so: of wind, fighting, trade, feeling or faith strong and intense, of a rule or a leader firm and strict; built on <khauh>, hard or strong
<khauhpai> with the noun suffix <na>: the being strong or intense of an earthquake, fighting and the like; {khauhpaina mun} is the place where it is strongest
<khauh> strong or stiff, <pen> most, with the plural <te>: the stiffest bows
<khauh>, hard or strong, with <sak>, make: make hard or make strong; {lungsim khauhsak} means harden the heart, and {khut khauhsak} means strengthen the hands
<khauhsak>, harden, with the linking suffix <in>
<khauhsak> harden, with <khak>, happen to; of hardening the heart
<khauhsak> with the noun suffix <na>: the act of making weak hands strong
<khauh>, hard or strict, and <semsem>, more and more, written as one word: firmer or stricter than before, said of security and of faith
noodles made from wheat flour; also instant noodles
<khauh> and <tak> written as one word, usually followed by <in>: firmly, strictly or severely; {khauhtak in thu bawl} is deal severely with a case
<khauh>, hard or firm, with <takin>, like English -ly: strongly, firmly or severely; of the Spirit of God coming on someone, powerfully
act in a hard way toward someone
<khauh> hard, strong, with the plural <te>; {lungsim khauhte} are the stout-hearted
of people compared to oak trees
a rope or cord made of twisted strands, used for tying and binding
<khauhual>, rope, with <pi>, large: a thick rope, such as a cart rope
<khauhual>, rope, with the plural <te>
<khauh> hard or strict, with <zaw> more; with <in> it is used as an adverb, more strictly
a cord hung with a weight to test whether a wall stands upright; {khaukhai sikbawk} is the weighted plumb line
<khau>, rope, and <khattawh>, with a, written as one word: with a rope

terms: tie with a rope/tie a rope to
definition: <khau>, rope, and <khih>, tie, written as one word: fasten a rope to something
<khau>, rope, with <khung>, put across: stretch a rope or tape, to close off a place or to hold on to
dense tangle of bushes or creepers, in which the ram was caught by its horns
